key_insight: Water in layered Andersson-Wadsley titanates self-organizes into 1D chains and hydrated surfaces, enabling fast anisotropic proton transport.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies a hydration-driven route to high room-temperature proton conductivity in titanate electrolytes, relevant for solid-state energy and membrane devices.
method: Scanning electron microscopy to map hydration-dependent microstructure
Density Functional Theory simulations to resolve water ordering and hydrogen bonding
Infrared spectroscopy to support densely packed hydrated (001) surface chains
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ordered 1D water chains at low hydration, hydrated (001) surfaces at higher hydration, and superionic proton conductivity reaching 3 mS/cm at room temperature along b in Rb2Ti2O5.
watch_item: Performance appears strongly dependent on crystal orientation and hydration level, so reproducible control of water content and surface state may be challenging in practice.
paper_title: One-dimensional self-organization of water molecules in proton conducting Andersson-Wadsley titanates
